A1.direct_sum_pairing: A1=sum_p sum_nu <c1_(p,nu),K1_(p,nu)> after the exact source tensor contraction.
A1.exact_grouped_kernel_definition: For each p,nu, K1_(p,nu)=(1/d')*sum_{k in I} exp(i*tau_k*lambda_nu)*sum_{a:p^a<=N,epsilon=+/-} Gamma_(p,a,epsilon;k)*exp(i*tau_k*epsilon*a*log(p)), tau_k=T+2*pi*k/L. Gamma is the actual realified source coefficient tensor with masks, lag/root/path factors and any k-dependent source gates; it excludes this displayed trace carrier, which occurs exactly once. Conjugates are included exactly once. All current powers/signs are combined at fixed p,nu before norming.
A1.mixture_bound: For feasible mu_p separately for each p, |A1|^2<=M1_R^2*(sum_p g_p^2)*D1_T, D1_T=sum_{p,nu}||K1_(p,nu)||^2/(g_p^2*W_(p,mu_p)(nu)).
A1.status: OPEN: no source-matched estimate of this full dual mass is available; contour averaging alone does not control the aliases or the p-sum.

A2.exact_grouped_kernel_definition: For each p,nu, K2_(p,nu)=(1/d')*sum_{k in I} exp(i*tau_k*lambda_nu)*sum_{a,b:p^a,p^b<=N,epsilon,epsilon'}' [Gamma_(p,a,epsilon;k) tensor Gamma_(p,b,epsilon';k)]*exp(i*tau_k*(epsilon*a+epsilon'*b)*log(p)), tau_k=T+2*pi*k/L. Each Gamma contains the actual realified mask/lag/root/path coefficient and any k-dependent gates but excludes the displayed carrier, so every carrier occurs once. The prime removes only epsilon'=-epsilon and a=b, exactly the Sigma_p diagonal; retain all other pairs.
A2.normalization: A2=(1/2)*sum_p sum_nu <c2_(p,nu),K2_(p,nu)> with K2 defined before the 1/2 factor.
A2.status: OPEN: fourth prime mass improves the sufficient target, but the full residual dual mass is not bounded.
A2.target: D2_T=o(L^4), not merely an unspecified polynomial bound.

alias_falsification.intermediate_far: The geometric kernel decay applies pointwise, but summing it against all actual response coefficients, paths, masks and p weights remains open.
alias_falsification.m_zero: For current exponent r!=0, p-adic valuation excludes lambda_nu+r*log(p)=0 by unique factorization.
alias_falsification.near: The sampled geometric kernel can be order one within O(1/T) of mL; contour weight suppresses a high-height coefficient but no total count/dual-mass estimate is proved.
alias_falsification.periodic: lambda_nu+r*log(p)=mL with m!=0 is possible; the retained primorial example is an admissible exact frequency label, not evidence its source coefficient is nonzero.

primorial_test.family: p=2,r=1, X_y=2*product_{3<=q<=y prime}q, nu_q=1 on odd primes q<=y, so lambda_nu+log(2)=log(X_y)=L_y.
primorial_test.interpretation: The exact alias kernel factor is one; under this mixture its individual reciprocal weight decays exponentially in L_y. This is a single-label statement and does not bound the full alias family or prove a nonzero response coefficient.
primorial_test.one_contour: For rho_q=(log q)/4, feasible once 32|S_y|/L_y<=131/400; this holds eventually because |S_y|/L_y~1/log y.
primorial_test.optimized_single_label_mixture: For this positive index, minimize the one-label dual term by maximizing 2*sum_q rho_q subject to sum B_q(rho_q)<=131/400. The unique optimizer has 1=mu*B_q'(rho_q) for every q in S_y and sum B_q(rho_q)=131/400; the point mass at that single feasible contour is an explicit common measure for this one-label truncation. This is not a common optimizer for other labels.
primorial_test.optimized_weight: W_opt=exp(2*sum_{q in S_y}rho_q^*) with rho_q^* defined by the preceding finite strictly-convex KKT system; no decimal optimizer is claimed.

contour_mixture.caveat: Probability averaging costs no factor on the Parseval right side, but the pointwise lower bound retains a support-size factor in reciprocal dual masses.
contour_mixture.finite_statement: For each feasible s, sum_{nu in F} exp(2*s.dot(nu))*||c_nu||^2<=M^2. Integrate any probability measure mu on the feasible contour body: sum_{nu in F} W_mu(nu)||c_nu||^2<=M^2, W_mu=integral exp(2*s.dot(nu)) dmu(s).
contour_mixture.infinite_statement: For increasing finite Fourier sets exhausting the countable index set, monotone convergence for nonnegative terms gives sum_nu W_mu(nu)||c_nu||^2<=M^2.

optimization.convexity: W_mu(nu) is affine and positive in mu; x->1/x is convex on x>0, hence D_mu is convex in mu.
optimization.existence: For finitely many active coordinates, the feasible contour body is compact and W_mu(nu) is bounded away from zero; a minimizing probability measure exists.
optimization.finite_support: If |F|=n, the vector (W_mu(nu))_{nu in F} lies in the convex hull of the compact feature set s->(exp(2*s.dot(nu)))_nu. Caratheodory gives a measure on at most n+1 feasible contours with the same objective value.
optimization.numerical_optimizer: None used; no numerical optimum is asserted.
optimization.warning: This is one common measure for the whole finite truncation. It does not permit selecting a different optimizer separately for each nu.

contour_mixture.pointwise_lower_bound: W_rho(nu)>=2^(-|supp(nu)|)*exp(2*sum_q rho_q*abs(nu_q)); equality factor 1/2 per nonzero coordinate is sharp as |2*rho_q*nu_q| tends to infinity.
contour_mixture.sign_mixture: Independent uniform signs on a fixed nonnegative feasible radius vector rho give W_rho(nu)=product_q cosh(2*rho_q*nu_q).

current_prime_mass.cube_mass: sum_{p<=N}g_p^3<=64*L^-3*sum_p log^3(p)/(sqrt(p)-1)^3=O(L^-3); the prime series converges.
current_prime_mass.envelope: g_p=4*log(p)/(L*(sqrt(p)-1)); ||V_p||<=g_p by summing every retained power and enlarging to the infinite geometric series.
current_prime_mass.fourth_mass: sum_{p<=N}g_p^4<=256*L^-4*sum_p log^4(p)/(sqrt(p)-1)^4=O(L^-4); the prime series converges.
current_prime_mass.max_mass: max_p g_p<=4*log(2)/(L*(sqrt(2)-1))=O(L^-1); x->log(x)/(sqrt(x)-1) decreases for x>=2.
current_prime_mass.normalization_caveat: This uses the exact source block envelope 4 log(p)/(L p^(a/2)); it is not the scalar coefficient envelope log(p)/(L sqrt(p)) with an omitted path/operator factor.
current_prime_mass.source_block_bound: ||B_(p^a)||<=4*log(p)/(L*p^(a/2)), including source vector/operator factors and the complete retained path block.
current_prime_mass.square_mass: sum_{p<=N} g_p^2 = (16/L^2)*sum_{p<=N} log^2(p)/(sqrt(p)-1)^2 = 8+o(1), hence O(1). Here (sqrt(p)-1)^(-2)=p^(-1)*(1+O(p^(-1/2))) and PNT gives sum_{p<=N}log^2(p)/p~(log N)^2/2, log N~L.

first_unproved_lemma: Prove D1_T=o(1) and D2_T=o(L^4) for the exact source-contracted grouped kernels, uniformly over the selected section and fixed R, including all nonzero periodic, near, intermediate and far aliases; no such source-matched total estimate is presently proved.

radius_schedule_tests.conclusion: These feasible schedules establish contour admissibility only. None proves D1=o(1) or D2=o(L^4) without an estimate for the actual kernel sums and growing-support multiplicities.
radius_schedule_tests.log_weighted_power_decay: rho_p=c/(sqrt(p)*log(p)^beta), beta>1: linearized cost is O(c/L)*sum_p 1/(p*log(p)^(beta-1)), convergent by PNT; high-prime height weight is weaker still.
radius_schedule_tests.logarithmic_shells: For a finite shell P_j, rho_p=eta_j*log(p), with sum_j 128*eta_j*|P_j|/L<=131/400; each shell budget is explicit, but summing the dual masses over all shell supports remains unproved.
radius_schedule_tests.power_decay: rho_p=c*p^(-alpha), alpha>1/2 and fixed c<=1/4: B_p(rho_p)<=C*c*log(p)/(L*p^(1/2+alpha)); the prime sum converges, so total cost O_c(1/L), but height gained is only c*sum |nu_p|*log(p)*p^(-alpha).
radius_schedule_tests.prime_square_mass: rho_p=c*log(p)/(L*sqrt(p)); linearized total cost is O(c/L^2)*sum_{p<=N}log^2(p)/p=O(c), so choose c from the exact B_p sum before use. This schedule gives only the influence-weighted height.
radius_schedule_tests.uniform_log_radius: rho_p=eta*log(p), eta=min(1/4,131*L/(51200*s)) on an index support of size s; certified total perturbation cost <=131/400. Useful for sparse/primorial supports, not all primes simultaneously with eta=1/4.
